<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/tmp/codex-home/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions><permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`: No filesystem sandboxing - all commands are permitted. Network access is enabled.
Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.
</permissions instructions><collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

<multi_agent_mode>Any earlier instruction enabling proactive multi-agent delegation no longer applies. Do not spawn sub-agents unless the user or applicable AGENTS.md/skill instructions explicitly ask for sub-agents, delegation, or parallel agent work.</multi_agent_mode>

# Improve the staged experiment

Review the staged experiment and determine whether it is healthy. Inspect the
source, launch script, metrics, rollouts and debug evidence. If you find a
defect, repair it in `/workspace`. Do not launch training; the system performs
the graded rerun after your response. Cheap non-training checks are allowed.

Write `/workspace/report.md` describing the root cause, every changed file and
the expected metric effect. A missing report scores zero.

The system deletes `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`, then runs:

```bash
bash run_experiment.sh
```

The fixed experiment must preserve the supplied Qwen2.5-0.5B PiSSA rank-8
bundle, deterministic GSM8K 16/8 subset, rollout n=4, response length 32,
temperature 0.8, KL coefficient 0.05, four GRPO updates, seed and one-GPU
layout. Do not add format reward or any auxiliary reward, and do not alter
data, model, budget or metric logging. The grader reads only fresh files under
`experiment_logs`: the final step-4 actor/rollout health metric, cross-checked
against verl's own per-step file log and the probe dumps the run writes, with
the launch script and the health instrumentation pinned by sha256. Copying or
fabricating metrics scores zero.
I’ll inspect the staged code, launch script, and saved evidence, then repair any defect and write `/workspace/report.md`. I’ll use only non-training checks.

import json
from pathlib import Path
import torch
from safetensors import safe_open

torch.set_num_threads(2)
bundle=Path('/workspace/assets/qwen2.5-0.5b-pissa-r8')
config=json.loads((bundle/'pissa_adapter/adapter_config.json').read_text())
scale=config['lora_alpha']/config['r']
squared_error=0.0
squared_missing_delta=0.0
count=0
max_error=0.0
with safe_open(str(bundle/'residual_base/model.safetensors'),framework='pt',device='cpu') as residual, \
     safe_open(str(bundle/'pissa_adapter/adapter_model.safetensors'),framework='pt',device='cpu') as adapter, \
     safe_open('/workspace/assets/source-qwen2.5-0.5b/model.safetensors',framework='pt',device='cpu') as source:
    for a_key in adapter.keys():
        if not a_key.endswith('.lora_A.weight'):
            continue
        module=a_key.removesuffix('.lora_A.weight')
        b_key=module+'.lora_B.weight'
        base_key=module.removeprefix('base_model.model.')+'.weight'
        a=adapter.get_tensor(a_key).float()
        b=adapter.get_tensor(b_key).float()
        w_res=residual.get_tensor(base_key).float()
        w=source.get_tensor(base_key).float()
        err=(w_res+scale*(b@a)-w)
        squared_error+=err.square().sum().item()
        squared_missing_delta+=(w_res-w).square().sum().item()
        max_error=max(max_error,err.abs().max().item())
        count+=err.numel()
print('Read-only bundle reconstruction; matrices=48, scalar weights=',count)
print('W_res + B A vs source RMS:',(squared_error/count)**0.5)
print('W_res alone vs source RMS:',(squared_missing_delta/count)**0.5)
print('Max reconstructed error:',max_error)
assert squared_error < squared_missing_delta*0.001

+# Staged experiment repair
+
+The recorded experiment is unhealthy. Its actor and rollout engine evaluate different policies. I repaired weight synchronization and adapter selection without running training.
+
+## Evidence reviewed
+
+- `run_experiment.sh`: the supplied Qwen2.5-0.5B PiSSA rank-8 residual-base/adapter bundle, deterministic GSM8K train/validation files, four GRPO updates, accuracy-only reward, and the prescribed sampling, KL, seed, and one-GPU settings.
+- `observed_run/metrics/all_steps.jsonl` and `observed_run/train.log`: at step 4, `val-health/actor_rollout_policy_mae` is **2.2560474629304847** and `val-health/actor_rollout_policy_agreement` is **0.10476375009925555**. Training `rollout_corr/kl` is **3.1912375688552856**, and mean rollout/actor probability difference is **0.10214164853096008**. All four updates have zero reward, advantages, policy loss, and gradient norm. Base-reference MAE is zero and consistency is 1.0.
+- Saved rollouts and validation generations: all eight step-0 validation responses contain `####`; none of the eight step-4 validation responses do. Later outputs are garbled or repetitive, such as `Rid is 40 1200000000000000000 120 1`. All saved scores are zero. This deterioration occurs even though the actor's recorded gradient norms are zero.
+- `observed_run/debug/unknown_exp.rollout_sync_initial.rank0.json` reports `svd_init_original_pretrained_full_weights` with no PEFT configuration. The latest-sync dump reports `lora_delta` with PEFT enabled. Actor dumps show the `default` adapter active; base-reference probes agree with the initial actor.
+- Source inspection covered the FSDP sync and reference paths, vLLM weight loading and request selection, actor log probabilities, and the final health calculation. The bundle has 96 adapter tensors targeting q/v projections at rank 8. Parquet metadata confirms 16 training rows and eight validation rows.
+
+## Root cause
+
+For PiSSA, the actor's effective weights are `W_res + delta_current`. The frozen reference is `W_res + delta_initial`, approximately the original pretrained weights. The residual base by itself is not the actor policy.
+
+Two connected defects break that relationship in rollout:
+
+1. The first SVD-adapter sync loads a separate original pretrained model and sends no adapter. Subsequent syncs use another representation: with vLLM sleep level 2, they restore the actor's residual base and register its current adapter. This changes what the rollout base means between initial validation and later generations. With a retained pretrained base, applying the adapter would instead double-count its initial contribution.
+2. `vLLMHttpServerBase.generate` checks `VLLM_LORA_NAME` (the string `"123"`) against `engine.list_loras()`, whose members are integer IDs. The check fails for the registered adapter ID `123`, so requests omit the adapter. After residual-base restoration, generation therefore runs `W_res`, while actor scoring runs `W_res + delta_current`.
+
+The zero base-reference error is consistent with the existing frozen-reference implementation working; it does not establish rollout agreement. Zero rewards and advantages explain the zero updates and should not be addressed by changing the reward.
+
+## Every changed or added file
+
+| File under `/workspace` | Change and expected effect |
+| --- | --- |
+| `verl/verl/workers/fsdp_workers.py` | Removes the original-pretrained first-sync branch and its unused loader. Always collects the current adapter separately; sends the actor's base before the adapter on initial sync and after sleep level 2. Uses the adapter-loading interface once the base is present. Initializes the tensor device independently of sync state. This keeps rollout at `W_res + delta_current` from its first generation onward, without merging into or modifying actor/reference tensors. |
+| `verl/verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/vllm_async_server.py` | Changes adapter membership lookup to `VLLM_LORA_INT_ID`, so requests actually apply the registered current adapter. The debug payloads and returned log probabilities are unchanged. |
+| `verl/tests/workers/rollout/test_pissa_policy_sync_on_cpu.py` | Adds seven CPU regression cases executing the source sync/generation methods with a small real PEFT model and fake transport/engine. Covers initial and repeated sync, preloaded and initially absent bases, sleep levels 1/2, changed adapter tensors, unchanged actor/frozen-reference tensors, and present/absent/unrelated adapter IDs. No training or experiment metrics are produced. |
+| `report.md` | This diagnosis, change inventory, validation record, and metric expectation. No runtime effect. |
+
+## Non-training validation
+
+`python -m pytest -q tests/workers/rollout/test_pissa_policy_sync_on_cpu.py -p no:cacheprovider` from `/workspace/verl`: **7 passed**. Ruff checks for the added test passed. Both changed source files parse successfully; `bash -n /workspace/run_experiment.sh` passed.
+
+A read-only CPU calculation across all 48 adapted projection matrices verified the supplied bundle: RMS error versus the original source weights is **0.0000463058** for `W_res + delta_initial`, versus **0.01234625** for `W_res` alone. The small reconstruction error reflects the saved low-precision tensors. No asset was rewritten.
+
+The local shell has older packages than `observed_run/environment-freeze.txt`; a full worker import encounters a missing `tensordict.utils.LinkedList`. The focused tests therefore compile the relevant source definitions and use real Torch/PEFT tensors without importing the distributed stack. They verify control flow and tensor equivalence, not an end-to-end GPU rerun. Training was not launched, and no fresh health metric is claimed.
+
+The launch script, all assets, all data, recorded evidence, trainer health calculation, actor loss/logging, and probe-writing code are preserved. In particular, the launch script SHA256 remains `a89653ef127c9d6ddf082c20b3d3593121b79f6fc21e65d8f1e9b1028603f040`; `verl/verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py` remains `4e2231b24b4b5b0381a012ea348d2f51e1666ec4f4a4cdd55953a20335d1d6f8`. No files were copied or written into `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`.
+
+## Expected fresh-run metrics
+
+Step-4 actor/rollout MAE should fall substantially from **2.2560**, and agreement (`exp(-MAE)`) should rise substantially from **0.1048**, toward 1. Exact equality is not promised: the unchanged instrumentation compares actor scores at rollout temperature 0.8 with greedy validation rollout log probabilities, and the two backends have numerical differences. Training rollout/actor discrepancy and KL diagnostics should also fall once both execute the same weights and adapter.
+
+Base-reference consistency should remain near **1.0**. Generations should recover the actor's behavior instead of residual-only corruption. Accuracy, nonzero advantages, or nonzero gradients are not guaranteed on this tiny subset with 32 response tokens and only four updates. The graded rerun must measure the actual effect from fresh logs and probes.
*** End Patch"));
